title: The restart loop on big databases
prompt: After a customer's database grew, notes-api's startup cache warm-up takes up to 90 seconds. Its liveness probe on `/healthz` uses the defaults (`periodSeconds: 10`, `failureThreshold: 3`), so Pods are killed at about 30 seconds and never finish starting. The `/healthz` handler isn't registered until warm-up completes. Which change is the best fix?
hints: You want generous patience during startup and quick detection of hangs afterwards. Which probe separates those two phases?
Count: how long does `periodSeconds × failureThreshold` need to be?
explanation:
A startup probe holds off liveness and readiness until it succeeds once. With `periodSeconds: 5` and `failureThreshold: 24`, notes-api gets up to 120 seconds to warm up, is detected as started within 5 seconds of finishing, and from then on liveness runs at its normal 10-second pace:

```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: http
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 24
```
`initialDelaySeconds` would work today but delays every start by the worst case and breaks again when warm-up hits 95 seconds.

startup.why: Correct. Up to 120 seconds to start, checked every 5 seconds, then liveness takes over unchanged.

initial-delay.why: It delays liveness by 90 seconds on every start, even fast ones, and fails again as soon as warm-up exceeds 90 seconds.

no-liveness.text: Remove the liveness probe; readiness is enough.
no-liveness.why: Readiness never restarts anything, so a deadlocked process would sit there forever, out of rotation but never fixed.

liveness-readyz.text: Point the liveness probe at `/readyz` instead.
liveness-readyz.why: That doesn't add startup time, and it ties restarts to database health, which turns database blips into outages.
